references.text: God reveals his name YHWH to Moses at the burning bush, which forms the basis for the revelation in 6:2.
God repeats the phrase 'I am the Lord' several times as confirmation of his identity and promises to Israel.
God reveals himself to Abraham with the words 'I am God Almighty', showing a pattern of divine self-revelation.
God reveals himself to Jacob as 'God Almighty', a similar self-revelation as in Exodus 6:2.
Ezekiel uses the phrase 'I am the Lord' when God reveals himself, reflecting the language from Exodus 6:2.
God proclaims 'I am the Lord; that is my name', confirming the same self-revelation as in Exodus 6:2.
Jesus uses the expression 'I am' (ἐγὼ εἰμί), which connects to God's self-revelation as YHWH in the Old Testament.
Direct continuation of the same conversation; 6:10 builds directly on God's self-presentation in 6:2.
